result.note: Tests Mission Drishti's optical-SAR first, its launch vehicle and the NSIL distribution tie-up.

questions.prompt: Consider the following statements about Mission Drishti, launched by the Bengaluru-based startup GalaxEye in May 2026:
items: It is the world's first satellite to combine optical and Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) imaging on a single platform.
It was launched aboard an ISRO Polar Satellite Launch Vehicle.
GalaxEye has partnered with NewSpace India Limited (NSIL) for global distribution of its imagery.
questions.ask: Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explain: Statement 2 is wrong because the 190 kg satellite was launched aboard a SpaceX Falcon 9, not an ISRO rocket. It is also India's largest privately built satellite, and NSIL, ISRO's commercial arm, will handle global distribution of the imagery.
questions.source: The 190 kg satellite is the world's first to combine optical and Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) imaging on a single platform, allowing all-weather, day-and-night Earth observation.
